title: Futures foretold (Kern ch. 6)
hook: the great disciples are told their future Buddha names and lands
tomorrow: The long story of a past Buddha (Kern ch. 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the rain on the plants: one rain fell on every plant, and each grew by its own nature, like one teaching heard by many. Your line: one rain, many plants. What did two different people do with the same kindness? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-nine.

At a graduation, the names are read out one at a time. Each person waits for theirs. Some are calm. Some are gripping the arm of the chair. And there's a moment, between one name and the next, when the people still waiting wonder if theirs is really on the list. Chapter six of the Lotus has that moment in it, except the list is of future Buddhas, and the ones waiting are some of the Buddha's closest disciples. Today: vyakarana.
screen: `NAMES READ ONE AT A TIME.` → `GRIPPING THE CHAIR.` → `IS MY NAME ON THE LIST?`

segments.voice: First, the word. Vyakarana is the Sanskrit word the Lotus uses for this kind of announcement: a prediction, a declaration, the Buddha saying out loud what someone's future will be. Sariputra received one in chapter three. Chapter six is named for it. Second, Kasyapa. The Buddha turns to Mahakasyapa, one of the disciples who told the story of the lost son, and declares that after honoring many Buddhas in ages to come, he will become a Buddha himself. Kern gives the name as Rasmiprabhasa, and the sutra describes his land: level, clean, with jeweled trees, free of rubble and thorns. Third, the waiting. Now the other great disciples, Subhuti, Katyayana and Maudgalyayana, are trembling. In Kern's translation they speak to the Buddha in verse with a picture worth keeping. We are like a man who has come out of a famine, they say, and finds a royal meal set in front of him. He is starving, but he does not dare to touch it until the king himself says: eat. They have heard that disciples can become Buddhas. They cannot quite believe it applies to them until the Buddha says so by name. Fourth, the names. And the Buddha does. One by one he declares each of them a future Buddha, gives each a Buddha name and describes each one's land and the long time their teaching will last. The sutra takes its time over every one, as if no one should be hurried past. That is the feel of vyakarana in the Lotus. It is not a horoscope. It doesn't tell you what will happen to you on Tuesday. It is a teacher looking at a student and saying, in front of everyone: I see where you are going, and I am sure of it. The starving man is allowed to eat.
screen: `VYAKARANA: A DECLARATION.` · `KASYAPA WILL BE A BUDDHA.` · `A STARVING MAN AT A ROYAL MEAL.` · `EACH ONE NAMED.` · then, large: `A FUTURE FORETOLD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: wish someone a bright future. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one person who might be waiting, quietly, to be told they'll be all right: a friend between jobs, a teenager, someone recovering. See them clearly. Then, silently, wish them well, in a few plain words of your own, about the road ahead of them. Hold the wish gently, the way you'd hold a meal out to someone hungry. Let them take it. The bell holds the time.
Vyakarana. A prediction or declaration: in the Lotus, the Buddha announcing that a disciple will become a Buddha, with a name and a land of their own. Today's word.
Your line: a future foretold. Today, when someone hesitates over something good that's offered to them, be the one who says: go ahead, it's yours. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-nine.

howItsDone: In Mahayana Buddhism a vyakarana is a Buddha's prediction that someone will reach Buddhahood; the Lotus Sutra gives a series of them, and some East Asian teachers read them as the one vehicle spoken to each hearer by name.

original.note: Sanskrit: a declaration or prediction; the title of chapter six in Kern's Sanskrit text.

trapdoor: what you thought: a fortune-teller's prediction.
what it means: the Buddha's public declaration that a disciple will become a Buddha, with a name and a land.
what a scholar hears: the Lotus's chain of predictions, from Sariputra on, applies the one vehicle to named people; chapter six is titled for the vyakarana itself.

notes: Chapter 6 paraphrased from Kern (SBE XXI, 1884); nothing quoted.

Check: Kasyapa's future name as Kern spells it (Rasmiprabhasa); the description of his land; the order of the other predictions; the famine/royal-meal simile in the disciples' verses. Kern gives the future names of Subhuti, Katyayana and Maudgalyayana and numbers of ages; not given here.
Vyakarana also means grammar in Sanskrit; left out under the claims rule.
